sources.citation: Benham-Chandler, Claire & Emily Gasser. 2016/2017. 'About the Pom Dictionary' (phonology/grammar notes). In: Gasser, Emily. 2016. Pom Talking Dictionary. Living Tongues Institute for Endangered Languages. http://talkingdictionary.swarthmore.edu/pom/about/
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Gives phoneme inventory (p t k b d m n ŋ β s h dʒ r j w; i e a o u), phonotactics (CV(C), homorganic NC clusters), i/u gliding, VRK mutation, verb agreement paradigms; closes 'The morphology and syntax of Pom remain almost entirely undescribed.' No mention of stress, accent or tone.

sources.citation: Kamholz, David C. 2014. Austronesians in Papua: Diversification and change in South Halmahera-West New Guinea. PhD dissertation, UC Berkeley.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Pom appears only in lexical/pronominal comparisons (sources: Silzer 1983, Anceaux 1961, ACD). Sec. 5.4 (pp. 117-118) lists SHWNG languages with described penultimate stress (Buli, Sawai, Taba, Ambai, Wandamen, Waropen, Warembori) and proposes Proto-SHWNG penultimate stress; Pom is not mentioned. Nothing on Pom stress.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Pom section D (pp. 6-7) has only grammatical remarks (no dual/trial pronouns, kinship possession). p. 14 on transcription: 'Stress-accent, vowel pitch and vowel length (part of the accentual system in many of these languages) are not indicated.' The only language given an accent remark is Papuma (p. 7, distinctive word accent). Nothing on Pom stress.
